column1: # docs/capability-review/g8-generation.md): a HOLE in a call, filled by
# whatever the call is unified with — and, inside a generator's
# template, by the source child the generated one is made FROM.
# BREAKING CHANGE, pinned here. A bare `_` used to be the string "_";
# it is a hole now. `"_"` quoted is still that string, a longer bare
# word containing it is still ordinary text, and `_` as a KEY is still
# a key — the four rows that say so are the compatibility contract.
# The peer goes INTO the call and is not also a constraint on the way
# out: `upper(_) & hello` is "HELLO", not "HELLO" & "hello". Two holes
# meeting is an error, because neither has a value to fill the other.
# A hole under a PREFERENCE: the generated default is the source
# child, still overridable per child. This is the row that reaches the
# pref arm of the fill walk, whose peg is a Val rather than a list of
# The fill walk reaches every shape a template can hold: a conjunct, a
# disjunct, a list, a nested map — and two placeheld OPERATORS meeting
# is the same refusal two placeheld calls are.
# A HOLE BELONGS TO ITS NEAREST ENCLOSING GENERATOR (ADR-005,
# 2026-08-26; use-cases/BUGS.md §34): an outer pack's fill pass used
# to fill a NESTED pack's template hole lexically, binding `_` to the
# OUTER source child — deploy.dev.services.web.v answered the env name
# "dev", exit 0. Each generator now fills only its own template's
# holes: the inner `_` is the inner generator's source child, both as
# a bare hole and as a meet operand. Parity-probed in both engines.
# A HOLE AS A GENERATOR'S DATA (the other side of the boundary): the
# hole in `each(_)` is in the DATA argument — a binding position it is
# NOT — so the OUTER pack's fill pass fills it with the outer source
# child, and the inner each() then iterates that child. The two-arg
# spelling pins that the inner TEMPLATE argument rides through the
# fill untouched. Parity-probed in both engines.
